```{r}
source("../_common.R")
```

I saw the [Posit's blog post](https://opensource.posit.co/blog/2026-09-30_introducing-shinyreact/) anouncing the `shinyreact` package and was curious what all the excitement was about. I've worked on a few [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/) apps, but couldn't really wrap my head around how Shiny + [React](https://react.dev/) R package would work.

I recently built a Shiny app-package for browsing [#TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday) datasets: [`ttdviewer`](https://mjfrigaard.github.io/ttdviewer/). I designed the UI so I could pick a dataset title, view the files in List, Summary, and Graphs (from [`inspectdf`](https://alastairrushworth.com/inspectdf/)). I can also download each dataset as a CSV, `parquet`, or in its original format. 

`ttdviewer` uses `bslib` (`page_sidebar()`, `sidebar()`, and `navset_tab()`). In this post I'll cover converting the UI to [`shinyreact`](https://posit-dev.github.io/shinyreact/), the parts of the conversion the documentation doesn't cover, and the few surprises I hit along the way.

## What is `shinyreact`?

`shinyreact` moves the UI *out* of R. The server still holds the reactive graph (`input`, `reactive()`, `req()`, and `bindEvent()` all behave as usual), but the page is a React client we write ourselves. The package supplies the plumbing between the two and no UI components.

`shinyreact` is pretty new (version 0.1.0), and the documentation calls it a pre-release, so it's not on CRAN:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
pak::pak("posit-dev/shinyreact/pkg-r")
```

The R side is small. `page_react()` replaces the UI function and serves a `ui.js` (and `ui.css`) from `src_dir`, and `reactive_output()` sends any R value to the client as JSON:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
ls("package:shinyreact")
#> [1] "page_bare"       "page_react"      "page_react_dep"  "page_react_html"
#> [5] "reactive_output" "send_message"    "wire_tap"
```

On the client, the hooks on `window.shinyreact` read and write Shiny values: `useShinyInput()` sets `input[[id]]`, `useShinyOutputValue()` reads a `reactive_output()`, and `ShinyOutput` and `ImageOutput` host classic Shiny outputs inside React. `ShinyModuleProvider` namespaces the hook ids, so Shiny modules still work.

The diagram below shows how values move between the two sides:

## Spike first

The documentation only shows R examples for `plotly` and `reactable`. It doesn't mention `listviewerlite`, `renderPlot()`, `downloadHandler()`, or serving the client from an installed R package. Those are four of the app's five outputs, so before touching the package I built a small prototype (a spike) to test each one with Netflix Titles (one file) and Space Launches (two files).

All four worked.

### Lists

`listviewerlite::listview()` returns HTML, so the server keeps `renderUI()`, and the client hosts it with the `shiny-html-output` class:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
output$list <- renderUI({
  req(data())
  listviewerlite::listview(data())
})
```

```{verbatim}
<ShinyOutput id="list" className="shiny-html-output" />
```

### Plots

`ImageOutput` is only documented for Python, but it follows the same contract as R's `renderPlot()`. The client reports its size through `.clientdata_output_<id>_width` and `_height`, and draws the image `renderPlot()` sends back. The `inspect_plot()` ggplots rendered unchanged:

```{verbatim}
<ImageOutput id={`plt_${p.value}`} width="100%" height="300px" />
```

### Downloads

`downloadHandler()` binds to an anchor with the `shiny-download-link` class, so a `ShinyOutput` with `tagName="a"` works:

```{verbatim}
<ShinyOutput
  id="download"
  tagName="a"
  className="btn btn-primary w-100 shiny-download-link"
  href=""
  target="_blank"
  download=""
>
  Download Data
</ShinyOutput>
```

The CSV download for Netflix Titles returned 3.0 MB, and the two file zip for Space Launches returned 104 KB.

### Packaging

`page_react()` passes `src_dir` to `page_react_dep()`, which builds an `htmltools::htmlDependency()` with a file source. File sources work from an installed package, so the built client belongs in `inst/www/`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
app_ui <- function() {
  shinyreact::page_react(
    useBusyIndicators(spinners = TRUE, pulse = TRUE),
    src_dir = system.file("www", package = "ttdviewer"),
    theme = bslib::bs_theme(version = 5),
    title = "#TidyTuesday Viewer"
  )
}
```

`bs_theme(version = 5)` keeps Bootstrap on the page, so the React components can use the same classes (`form-select`, `nav-tabs`, `card`) the `bslib` UI used.

## The conversion

The conversion lives on its own branch, so `main` keeps the `bslib` app. The spike was built outside the repo, so the branch starts with the full conversion in one commit (`0dbf03e`). The graph below shows how the two branches relate:

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-width: 6
%%| fig-align: 'center'
%%{init: {'theme': 'base', 'gitGraph': {'mainBranchName': 'main', 'showCommitLabel': true, 'rotateCommitLabel': false}, 'themeVariables': { 'fontFamily': 'monospace', "darkMode":false, 'git0': '#4CBB9D', 'git1': '#E83E8C', 'gitBranchLabel0': '#FFFFFF', 'gitBranchLabel1': '#FFFFFF', 'commitLabelFontSize': '12px'}}}%%

gitGraph LR:
    commit id: "91bc354: zip support, 2026 data"

    commit id: "ab7a2e3: TidyTuesday date"
    commit id: "7202318: data vignette"
    branch shinyreact
    checkout shinyreact
    commit id: "0dbf03e: convert UI to shinyreact" type: HIGHLIGHT

    checkout main
    commit id: "c03fa33: tab order (bslib)"
    checkout shinyreact
    commit id: "5f4a1df: tab order (React)"
```

The branches don't share UI code anymore, so a UI change has to be made twice. Reordering the tabs (Summary, Graphs, List) took one commit on `main` (`R/app_ui.R`) and another on `shinyreact` (`js/src/ui.tsx`, then a rebuilt `inst/www/ui.js`).

### The client

The client lives in `js/`, a Vite and TypeScript (TSX) project. `npm run build` writes `inst/www/ui.js` and `ui.css`. React isn't bundled, because `shinyreact.js` (served by the R package) already provides it, so Vite maps `react` to the global `shinyreact.React`:

```{verbatim}
rollupOptions: {
  external: ["react"],
  output: { globals: { react: "shinyreact.React" } },
},
```

`js/` is in `.Rbuildignore`, and the built bundle is committed, so installing the package doesn't require Node.

The path from source files to the browser looks like this:

```{mermaid}

%%| fig-align: 'center'
```

### The modules

Every `mod_*_ui()` function is gone. Each server module keeps its id, and the client wraps the matching component in a `ShinyModuleProvider` with the same namespace:

```{verbatim}
<ShinyModuleProvider namespace="input">
  <TitleInput />
</ShinyModuleProvider>
```

The namespace strings on the client have to match the module ids in `app_server()`:


Plain values (the dataset titles, file names, and the Summary file overview) moved to `reactive_output()`. For example, `mod_input_server()` used to get its choices from `selectInput()` in the UI module. Now it sends them:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
output$titles <- shinyreact::reactive_output(
  unique(all_tt_combined$title)
)
```

And `TitleInput.tsx` reads the titles and sends the selection back as `input$ds_title`:

```{verbatim}
const titles = asArray(useShinyOutputValue<string | string[]>("titles", []));
const [title, setTitle] = useShinyInput("ds_title", "Space Launches");
```

The table below maps each module to its outputs and client component:

| Module | R output | Client |
|---|---|---|
| `mod_input` | `titles` (`reactive_output()`) | `TitleInput.tsx` |
| `mod_download` | `download` (`downloadHandler()`) | `Download.tsx` |
| `mod_list` | `list` (`renderUI()`) | `ListTab.tsx` |
| `mod_summary` | `overview`, `choices` (`reactive_output()`); `stats`, `vars`, `table` (`renderReactable()`) | `SummaryTab.tsx` |
| `mod_plot` | `datasets` (`reactive_output()`); `plt_<type>` (`renderPlot()`) | `GraphsTab.tsx` |

### `mod_plot_server()`

The plot module changed the most. The `bslib` version populated a dataset `selectInput()` with `updateSelectInput()`, created `renderPlot()` calls inside an observer, and built the plot containers with `renderUI()`. It also piped `return(...)` into `bindEvent()`, so the `bindEvent()` never ran.

The new version creates one `renderPlot()` per plot type up front, and each one is gated by `req()`:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
purrr::walk(PLOT_TYPES, function(plt) {
  output[[paste0("plt_", plt)]] <- renderPlot({
    req(plt %in% input$plots)
    ds <- selected() #<1> 
    tryCatch(
      inspect_plot(ttd = ds, plots = plt),
      error = function(err) {
        plot.new()
        text(0.5, 0.5, "Error generating plot", cex = 1.2, col = "red")
      }
    )
  })
})
```
1. outside `tryCatch()` so `req()` is not caught as an error

The checkboxes and plot containers now live in `GraphsTab.tsx`, and `PLOT_TYPES` has to match in both places.

## Surprises

### Length one vectors

`reactive_output()` passes the R value through unchanged, and Shiny serializes it with `auto_unbox`, so a character vector of length one arrives as a string, not an array.

The spike's server sent the file names and the TidyTuesday date for the selected title:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
output$files <- reactive_output({
  if (is.null(input$title)) return(NULL)
  d <- data()
  list(names = names(d), date = format(attr(d[[1]], "date")))
})
```

And the client joined the names into a single line:

```{verbatim}
files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", files.names.join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date),
```

The spike's default title was Netflix Titles, which has one file. The app crashed on load, and the browser console showed:

```{verbatim}
TypeError: files.names.join is not a function
    at App (http://localhost:8765/spike-1795198398/ui.js:20:61)
    at vf (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:47833)
    at Yf (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:70472)
    at Gd (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:80765)
    at ry (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:116187)
    at Kr (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115267)
    at uc (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:115104)
    at cy (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:111963)
    at My (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:40:123483)
    at MessagePort.It (http://localhost:8765/shinyreact-0.1.1/shinyreact.js:17:1579)
```

Shiny's internal `toJSON()` shows why. One file arrives as a string, and two files arrive as an array:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
# one file (Netflix Titles)
shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("netflix_titles.csv")))
#> {"names":"netflix_titles.csv"}

# two files (Space Launches)
shiny:::toJSON(list(names = c("agencies.csv", "launches.csv")))
#> {"names":["agencies.csv","launches.csv"]}
```

The spike fixed the client line with `[].concat()`, which turns a string into a one element array and leaves an array alone:

```{verbatim}
files && h("p", { id: "files" }, "Files: ", [].concat(files.names).join(", "), " | TidyTuesday date: ", files.date),
```

We can also protect the vector on the server with `I()`, which keeps it an array:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: false
shiny:::toJSON(list(names = I("netflix_titles.csv")))
#> {"names":["netflix_titles.csv"]}
```

Or we can wrap it on the client, so every `reactive_output()` is covered. In the package, I went with a small client helper:

```{verbatim}
export function asArray<T>(x: T | T[] | null | undefined): T[] {
  if (x === null || x === undefined) return [];
  return Array.isArray(x) ? x : [x];
}
```

### Outputs that never rendered

`app_server()` has a `dev` output (a `listview()` of the reactive values) in a closed `<details>` element in the sidebar. In the `bslib` UI it never rendered. Inside React it does, and `listviewerlite::listview()` errors on `NULL` elements (before a title loads). It now drops them with `purrr::compact()`.

### No type to search

The title picker is a native `<select>`, so it lost the type to search behavior `selectize` gave `selectInput()`. With 422 titles that's noticeable, and it's the main thing I'm still deciding on.

## Recap

The server barely changed: the modules kept their ids, `downloadHandler()`, `renderPlot()`, `renderUI()`, and `renderReactable()` all work inside React, and the busy indicators still show. What changed is where the UI lives (`js/` builds into `inst/www/`), and how plain values get to it (`reactive_output()`). The test suite went from 178 to 164 tests, because the UI module tests were dropped with the functions they tested.

The conversion is on the `shinyreact` branch for now. `shinyreact` is pre-release, so before merging I need the pkgdown GitHub Action to install it from `Remotes`, and a decision on the title picker.
